corrections.issue: Overstates the UK point. Andurand said UK prices are already at least double last year's, so some price response exists, and the problem is that more is needed from government awareness campaigns, not that the cap by itself leaves demand far above supply. He also gave France's regulated rise as 4% this year and 15% next year, not only 4%, and described the UK rise as retail prices doubling rather than a 'wholesale pass-through'.
corrections.fix: Governments must ensure demand meets supply, otherwise shortages and blackouts follow; France's regulated electricity and gas prices are up only 4% (15% next year), far below wholesale, while UK consumer prices have at least doubled so some price response is already in place, but more demand reduction is needed.

completeness_estimate: 0.88 - first reader caught the gas balance numbers, price cap mechanics, SPR and oil supply arithmetic and illiquidity themes; missed secondary mechanisms (weather, revenue denial, historical thermostat analogue, French nuclear recovery, thin-market skew, oil-vs-coal switching)
